readings.text: וַ/יֵּצֵ֤א אִֽישׁ הַ/בֵּנַ֨יִם֙ מִ/מַּחֲנ֣וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים גָּלְיָ֥ת שְׁמ֖/וֹ מִ/גַּ֑ת גָּבְה֕/וֹ שֵׁ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת וָ/זָֽרֶת־׃
καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἀνὴρ δυνατὸς ἐκ τῆς παρατάξεως τῶν ἀλλοφύλων Γολιαθ ὄνομα αὐτῷ ἐκ Γεθ ὕψος αὐτοῦ τεσσάρων πήχεων καὶ σπιθαμῆς
[הבנים ממערכות פלשתיים גלית שמו מגת גבהו ]א֯רבע[ א]מות וזרת

cases.observation: The versioned 4Q51 transcription directly preserves the decisive numeral as ]א֯רבע[, with an uncertain alef and the remaining letters visible; it does not expose the reconstructed surrounding words as ink. The Rahlfs Greek control also reads four cubits and a span, while WLC reads six. Greek agreement is related daughter-version evidence, not a second Hebrew manuscript.
cases.english_effect: The existing working preference for four now has a pinned direct-manuscript transcription and a pinned Greek edition control. The current WLC-aligned English remains unchanged until the image, DJD discussion, broader Samuel literary form, and atomic source/English promotion gates are complete.

readings.text: [אם יש בי] או ב֯[יונתן בני העון]

cases.observation: The Qumran-Digital transcription assigns 4Q52 fragment 2 to this passage and places most of the long prayer in brackets, including Urim and Thummim. The short unbracketed sequence is a published reading, not our image observation. Yardney's later identification challenge prevents using this fragment as secure Hebrew support without adjudicating the dispute. Her 2017 dissertation accepted broad support but already warned against circularly deriving the exact Hebrew from the Greek-informed reconstruction. The pinned Greek control's actual words and its Hebrew retroversion must remain separate.
cases.english_effect: Keep the present source-aligned wording as an interim baseline, not a judgment that the shorter prayer is original. Move the textual note to the prayer and disclose the supplied English word 'lot', longer Greek form, and disputed 4Q52 identification. Do not import the reconstructed Hebrew prayer or claim visible Urim/Thummim in this fragment.

readings.locator: fragment 3, line 5; QDR assigns traces to 21:19, but the published line links its supplied beginning to 21:18

cases.observation: The WLC Samuel source and pinned Greek control name Goliath as Elhanan's opponent. Chronicles names Lahmi, Goliath's brother, in a distinct parallel composition; it is not another Samuel manuscript. QDR's 1Q7 hit does not yield the disputed names: the versioned transcription has two isolated lameds after supplied material linked to verse 18. Their allocation within verse 19 is not securely established by this pass. This fragment cannot decide Goliath versus Lahmi or the patronymic.
cases.english_effect: Retain the current source-aligned Samuel wording while improving the notes and attaching each to its actual phrase. Do not import 'brother of' from Chronicles to remove the narrative tension. The possibility of corruption and the direction of literary change remain open, not decided by assuming harmonization.

readings.locator: fragments 2a-d, line 7, excerpt ending before deleted illegible signs
62008, 01:24, animal-to-flour sequence; 01:25 checked separately for short narrative
printed page 4, 1:24, bottom Hexaplaric apparatus: sigma-prime reading in z (Rahlfs 554), not its continuous text

cases.observation: The published 4Q51 line preserves בקר משלש ולחם; בפר בן is supplied. The whole clause is not recovered. The Rahlfs and Cambridge Vaticanus-based controls have an age-related bull and bread; they are overlapping edition evidence, not independent votes. Cambridge's separate Hexaplaric apparatus reports Symmachus's three bulls in z (Rahlfs 554), not that manuscript's continuous-text reading. CAL's Leiden-derived Syriac text has an age-related singular bull, immediately followed by flour, without bread, and retains a short verse 25. CAL glosses twlt as an animal-age term here but cautions about the term's interpretation; exact Hebrew retroversion and possible Greek influence remain unresolved. WLC has three bulls without bread. A simple respacing of the extant WLC consonants does not produce the alternative: spelling differences and the longer herd expression must also be explained. DJD XVII pages 31–35 located PAM 43.122 / IAA B-277400; the partial context-informed image check is consistent with the published age word and bread, not new recovery. The coverage receipt and Samuel pass 3 report preserve provenance and open gates. Animal, bread, and narrative form must be judged separately without losing their passage-level relationships.
cases.english_effect: The age-related alternative merits a source-selection dossier, but the whole offering/narrative unit must be assessed before promotion; do not silently combine a changed bull phrase with an unexamined literary form. The note now identifies the Hebrew and Greek support and bread plus. The present WLC-aligned sentence remains unchanged apart from its marker, and the unsupported harmonization claim is removed from the lexical rationale.
